x.t: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth
b: NASA worked out that Voyager 1 would reach one [[light-day|light-day]] from Earth on Wednesday. It is the first spacecraft to get this far.
A light-day is a distance: how far light travels in one day. Now a radio [[signal|signal]] takes about a day to reach Voyager 1. Its reply takes another day to come back.
Another spacecraft, Voyager 2, is expected to get this far in 2035.

o.t: Voyager 1 is the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
b: NASA worked out that its Voyager 1 spacecraft would reach one [[light-day|light-day]] from Earth on Wednesday 18 November. No human-made object has travelled this far before. Launched on 5 September 1977, it became the first spacecraft to enter [[interstellar|interstellar space]], the space between the stars, in 2012.

A light-day is a measure of distance, not time: how far light travels in 24 hours, about 25.9 billion kilometres. A radio [[signal|signal]] now takes about 24 hours, or one day, to reach Voyager 1, and its reply takes another day.

Voyager 1 is tracked by NASA's [[deep-space-network|Deep Space Network]], which has giant radio [[antenna|antennas]] in California, near Madrid in Spain and near Canberra in Australia. Most of its instruments have been switched off to save power. Voyager 2 is expected to reach one light-day in 2035.

stories.think: If a message took a whole day to arrive, what would you want to say in it, and why?

quiz.q: About how long does a radio signal now take to reach Voyager 1?

x.t: Helpers stay ready as forecasters update storm Akvan's path
b: National rescue teams in [[andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] are ready for the [[cyclone|cyclone]] Akvan.
On Wednesday, [[imd|India's weather office]] gave a new forecast. Akvan is likely to cross the coast onto land around noon on Friday. Earlier forecasts said it would cross further south.
The newest forecast expects lower winds, but forecasts can change. Families can follow updates. Odisha has paused beach trips and boat rides in some places.

o.t: Akvan's expected crossing area moves north as helpers stand by
b: [[andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] has national disaster response teams, called [[ndrf|NDRF]] teams, ready for [[cyclone|Cyclone]] Akvan.

On Wednesday the [[imd|IMD]], India's weather office, said Akvan was likely to cross the coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha by around noon on Friday 20 November. Earlier forecasts said it would cross further south. Akvan is now a severe cyclonic storm, the IMD's name for a stronger level of storm. The IMD's Wednesday update expects winds of 90 to 100 kilometres an hour as it crosses, lower than earlier forecasts. Some other forecasts on Wednesday were higher, and forecasts can still change.

Officials in Odisha ordered beach tourism, boating and water sports to be suspended, or paused, at some coastal spots. In Rayagada district, about 55 villages where landslides are likely have been identified so people can be moved before the storm. Officials say they are closely watching Akvan's movement.

stories.think: Why do you think forecasters keep updating their forecast as a storm moves?

quiz.q: On which day is Akvan likely to cross the coast?

o.t: Indian electric three-wheeler company among Earthshot winners
b: Five winners of the 2026 [[earthshot-prize|Earthshot Prize]], an environmental prize founded by Prince William, were named at an Awards Night in [[mumbai|Mumbai]], India, on Tuesday 17 November.

One winner is Indian: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, which won in the Clean Our Air category, one of the prize's groups of awards. It makes [[electric-three-wheeler|electric three-wheelers]], also called electric rickshaws. Electric three-wheelers can help reduce air pollution, or dirty air, on roads.
The other four winners are the country of Bhutan, PFAS-Free France, Niue Ocean Wide Trust and Ørsted. Each of the five winners will receive £1 million, or one million British pounds.

stories.think: One of the winners is a whole country, Bhutan. Why might a prize for the planet go to a whole country, and not just to one person or company?

x.t: India come from behind to win a record 10th SAFF title
b: India's football team won the [[saff-championship|SAFF Championship]] on Tuesday. They beat Pakistan 2-1 in the final in [[dhaka|Dhaka]], Bangladesh.
Pakistan scored first. In the second half, Suhail Bhat scored for India. Sandip Mandi scored the winning goal late in the match.
India have now won this contest 10 times, more than any other team. It is also their third win in a row.

o.t: India beat Pakistan 2-1 to win a record 10th SAFF Championship
b: India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the final of the [[saff-championship|SAFF Championship]], a football tournament, in [[dhaka|Dhaka]], Bangladesh, on Tuesday 17 November. It is India's 10th title in the competition, a record.

Pakistan took the lead through Alamgir Ghazi at the end of the first half, so India were 1-0 down at half-time. In the second half, Pakistan's Junaid Shah was sent off with a red card after a [[var|VAR]] review, for a challenge on India's Brison Fernandes. VAR is a system in which match officials watch video replays to check the referee's decisions. Pakistan finished the match with 10 players.
Suhail Bhat scored the equaliser, the goal that made the score level at 1-1. Sandip Mandi then scored the winning goal late in the match. It is India's third title in a row.

stories.think: India were losing at half-time but came back to win. What do you think helps a team keep trying when they are behind?

quiz.q: What was the score in the final?

x.t: Cambridge Dictionary picks "human" as its word of the year
b: Cambridge Dictionary has picked "human" as its 2026 Word of the Year.
The dictionary says human means having the qualities, faults and feelings people have. It says this sets people apart from gods, animals or machines.
It chose the word because of a debate about [[ai|AI]]. AI can make it hard to tell people and machines apart. A [[lexicographer|dictionary writer]] said AI is changing how we talk about being human.

o.t: Cambridge Dictionary names "human" its Word of the Year 2026
b: Cambridge Dictionary has named "human" its Word of the Year 2026. It announced the choice on Wednesday 18 November. The dictionary defines human as "having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines."

The dictionary said it chose the word because of debate about [[ai|artificial intelligence]], or AI, the ability of computers and other machines to do things thought to need intelligence, such as understanding spoken language or making decisions. There is a lot of debate about how AI is blurring the line between people and machines.
Colin McIntosh is a [[lexicographer|lexicographer]], a person who writes dictionaries, at Cambridge Dictionary. He said: "AI is changing how we talk about being human."

stories.think: What do you think people can do that machines cannot?

quiz.q: Which word did Cambridge Dictionary pick as its Word of the Year 2026?

x.t: Delhi lifts some air pollution rules as the air gets better
b: Delhi has a plan for air pollution, called [[grap|GRAP]]. Its rules come in stages. The air got better, so the Stage 3 rules have ended. The rules from Stages 1 and 2 stay in place.
Schools in Delhi can go back to regular classes. Building work that makes dust is still limited.
Forecasters say the cleaner air may not last.

o.t: Delhi lifts Stage III air rules, but other limits stay in place
b: The [[caqm|Commission for Air Quality Management]] (CAQM), the body that gives orders under Delhi's air pollution plan, has lifted Stage III of the [[grap|Graded Response Action Plan]] (GRAP). Graded means set out in steps, and GRAP's rules come in stages. Stage III was lifted because the air in Delhi got better.

Rules under Stages I and II stay in force. Curbs, or limits, on construction and demolition work that raises dust also continue. Demolition means knocking buildings down. Delhi's schools can go back to regular classes.
So the plan works in steps: this time, better air meant one stage of rules could be lifted while the earlier stages stayed. But forecasters say the cleaner air may not last.

stories.think: Why might a city have different levels of rules for air pollution, instead of one set of rules all the time?

quiz.q: What can Delhi's schools do now?

x.t: Norway come back from 2-0 down to beat Denmark
b: Norway beat Denmark 3-2 in a football match on Tuesday. At first, Denmark were winning 2-0.
[[haaland|Erling Haaland]] scored for Norway before half-time. Then Martin Ødegaard made it 2-2 late on.
In the last seconds, a video check found a handball by Denmark. Norway got a [[penalty|penalty]], and Haaland scored it. Norway are now in the quarter-finals. The draw for that round is on Friday.

o.t: Norway beat Denmark 3-2 with Haaland's last-second penalty
b: Norway came back from 2-0 down to beat Denmark 3-2 in the [[nations-league|UEFA Nations League]], a competition between the national teams of Europe, on Tuesday 17 November. The win sends Norway into the quarter-finals.
Rasmus Højlund and Pierre-Emile Højbjerg scored Denmark's goals. [[haaland|Erling Haaland]] scored for Norway before half-time, and Martin Ødegaard scored late on to make it 2-2.

The winning [[penalty|penalty]], a free shot at goal, came in the last seconds of stoppage time, the minutes added on at the end of a match. It was given for a handball by Denmark's Joachim Andersen, after a [[var|VAR]] review, a video check of the referee's decision. Haaland scored it. The draw for the quarter-finals, which decides who plays whom, is on Friday.

stories.think: A penalty in the last seconds decided this match. How do you think players stay calm when the whole game depends on one kick?

x.t: AI chip maker Nvidia's sales more than double
b: Nvidia is a company that makes computer chips used for [[ai|AI]]. On Tuesday, it said how much it sold in three months.
Its sales came to $115.8 billion. That is more than double the year before. Most of the money came from chips for data centres, buildings full of computers.
Nvidia forecast sales of about $130 billion for the next three months.

o.t: Nvidia's sales more than double to $115.8 billion
b: Nvidia, a company that makes computer chips used for [[ai|artificial intelligence]] (AI), released its results on Tuesday 17 November. They cover the [[quarter|quarter]], or three months, that ended on 25 October 2026.

Nvidia's [[revenue|revenue]], the money it gets from sales, was $115.8 billion. That is up 103 per cent from a year earlier, which means it more than doubled. Most of it, $107.6 billion, came from Nvidia's Data Center business, which sells chips for data centres, buildings full of powerful computers.
Nvidia forecast revenue of about $130 billion for the next quarter. A forecast is a best guess, so the real figure could turn out higher or lower.

stories.think: Nvidia told everyone how much it expects to sell in the next three months. Why do you think a company shares a forecast like this?

quiz.q: How much did Nvidia sell in the three months to 25 October?

x.t: Why do we have time zones?
b: Long ago, each town set its clocks by the Sun. So nearby towns had different times.
That was hard for railways. Their timetables got very muddled.
In 1883, railways in the United States started using time zones. Places in the same zone could then share the same time.
x.remember: A time zone is an area where everyone uses the same clock time.
x.q: How did towns set their clocks long ago?

o.t: Why do we have time zones?
b: Before the 1880s, each town in the United States kept its own local time, based on the position of the Sun. Clocks in towns not far apart could show different times.

This made life hard for the railways, which had to run trains to timetables across many towns. On 18 November 1883, railways in the United States switched to a new system of standard time zones. Clocks were reset at noon, so some places had noon twice that day. It was called the Day of Two Noons.
In 1918, the United States Congress made standard time law in the Standard Time Act. Time zones still organise clocks today.
o.remember: Time zones began with the railways: on 18 November 1883, railways in the United States switched to standard time.
o.q: Why was 18 November 1883 called the Day of Two Noons?

backThen.t: The first push-button telephone service begins
backThen.o: On 18 November 1963, the Bell telephone company began offering the world's first commercial service for touch-tone telephones, which have push buttons instead of a dial. The service started with customers in Carnegie and Greensburg, in Pennsylvania in the United States.
backThen.x: On this day in 1963, people could first pay for a phone service that used push buttons. Before that, phones had a dial. The first customers lived in two towns in the United States.
backThen.why: Over the next few decades, push buttons replaced dials, and all of today's phones still use the touch-tone system to dial numbers.
